HV: biz_days_add: Whenever a start date and a number of days n are given, the result is the ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) reached by moving n business days forward from the start date, counting Monday to Friday only.
biz_days_add: Whenever a day is skipped, it is because it is a Saturday, a Sunday, 25 December or 1 January (these two dates are holidays in every year); no other holidays exist.

biz_days_add: Whenever n is negative, the date moves backward by that many business days, skipping weekends, 25 December and 1 January the same way (e.g. Monday 2024-03-04 minus 1 gives Friday 2024-03-01).

biz_days_add: Whenever the start date falls on a Saturday or Sunday, it is first moved forward to the following Monday before counting, for positive, zero and negative n alike (Saturday 2024-03-02 plus 1 gives Tuesday 2024-03-05; Sunday 2024-03-03 minus 1 gives Friday 2024-03-01).
biz_days_add: Whenever n is 0 and the start date is a weekday, the start date is returned unchanged; when n is 0 and the start is a weekend, the next Monday is returned.

biz_days_add: Whenever the start date is itself 25 December or 1 January on a weekday, it is not moved and is returned as is for n = 0; counting then starts from that day (2024-12-25 plus 0 gives 2024-12-25, plus 1 gives 2024-12-26).
biz_days_add: Whenever a weekend start date is moved to Monday and that Monday is 25 December or 1 January, the holiday date is returned as is for n = 0 (2028-12-23 plus 0 gives 2028-12-25).
biz_days_add: Whenever n has a fractional part, it is cut toward zero before counting (2.9 counts as 2, -2.9 as -2, 0.5 and -0.5 as 0).
biz_days_add: Whenever n is text that is wholly a number (e.g. '3', ' 3 ' with spaces, or '1e1' meaning 10), it is used as that number.
biz_days_add: Whenever the start date or n is NULL, the result is NULL.
biz_days_add: Whenever n is text that is not a number (including empty text), the result is NULL, even if the start date is also invalid.

biz_days_add: Whenever the start date is not exactly four digits, hyphen, two digits, hyphen, two digits, or is not a real calendar date, the result is the text BAD_DATE; this covers '2024-02-30', '2024-2-3', empty text, a date with a time ('2024-03-01 10:00'), a date with leading spaces, and a plain number such as 20240301 (provided n is valid).
biz_days_add: Whenever the counting would go past the supported calendar range (before year 1 or after 9999-12-31, e.g. 9999-12-30 plus 5, or a huge n like 1e30), the result is the text BAD_DATE.

  1. biz_days_add: Whenever a start date and a number of days n are given, the result is the ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) reached by moving n business days forward from the start date, counting Monday to Friday only.
  2. biz_days_add: Whenever a day is skipped, it is because it is a Saturday, a Sunday, 25 December or 1 January (these two dates are holidays in every year); no other holidays exist.
  3. biz_days_add: Whenever n is negative, the date moves backward by that many business days, skipping weekends, 25 December and 1 January the same way (e.g. Monday 2024-03-04 minus 1 gives Friday 2024-03-01).
  4. biz_days_add: Whenever the start date falls on a Saturday or Sunday, it is first moved forward to the following Monday before counting, for positive, zero and negative n alike (Saturday 2024-03-02 plus 1 gives Tuesday 2024-03-05; Sunday 2024-03-03 minus 1 gives Friday 2024-03-01).
  5. biz_days_add: Whenever n is 0 and the start date is a weekday, the start date is returned unchanged; when n is 0 and the start is a weekend, the next Monday is returned.
  6. biz_days_add: Whenever the start date is itself 25 December or 1 January on a weekday, it is not moved and is returned as is for n = 0; counting then starts from that day (2024-12-25 plus 0 gives 2024-12-25, plus 1 gives 2024-12-26).
  7. biz_days_add: Whenever a weekend start date is moved to Monday and that Monday is 25 December or 1 January, the holiday date is returned as is for n = 0 (2028-12-23 plus 0 gives 2028-12-25).
  8. biz_days_add: Whenever n has a fractional part, it is cut toward zero before counting (2.9 counts as 2, -2.9 as -2, 0.5 and -0.5 as 0).
  9. biz_days_add: Whenever n is text that is wholly a number (e.g. '3', ' 3 ' with spaces, or '1e1' meaning 10), it is used as that number.
  10. biz_days_add: Whenever the start date or n is NULL, the result is NULL.
  11. biz_days_add: Whenever n is text that is not a number (including empty text), the result is NULL, even if the start date is also invalid.
  12. biz_days_add: Whenever the start date is not exactly four digits, hyphen, two digits, hyphen, two digits, or is not a real calendar date, the result is the text BAD_DATE; this covers '2024-02-30', '2024-2-3', empty text, a date with a time ('2024-03-01 10:00'), a date with leading spaces, and a plain number such as 20240301 (provided n is valid).
  13. biz_days_add: Whenever the counting would go past the supported calendar range (before year 1 or after 9999-12-31, e.g. 9999-12-30 plus 5, or a huge n like 1e30), the result is NULL.
  14. late_fee: Whenever days_late is 3 or fewer (including 0 and negative values), the fee is 0 (a grace period).

  17. late_fee: Whenever the fee is not a whole number of cents, it is rounded up to the next whole cent (10001 cents at 4 days gives 201; 999 cents at 4 days gives 20; 1 cent at 4 days gives 1).
  18. late_fee: Whenever days_late has a fractional part and is above 3, the fraction counts (3.5 days on 10000 cents gives 175); 3.0001 days is above the grace period and is charged (100 cents gives 2).
  19. late_fee: Whenever amount_cents is 0, the fee is 0; whenever it is negative and days_late is over 3, the fee is negative at the same percentage, rounded up toward zero (-10000 cents at 10 days gives -500; at 100 days gives -2500); with 3 days or fewer the fee is 0.

  21. late_fee: Whenever either input is NULL, empty text or text that is not a number, the result is NULL.

  23. letter_grade: Whenever the score has a half-point at a boundary, it rounds up into the higher grade (89.5 gives A, 79.5 gives B, 69.5 gives C, 59.5 gives D), while 89.49 gives B and 59.49 gives F.
  24. letter_grade: Whenever the score is exactly 0, between 0 and 0.5, or exactly 100, the grade is F for 0 to 59.49 and A for 100.
  25. letter_grade: Whenever the raw score is below 0 (even -0.1 or -0.4) or above 100 (even 100.5), the result is the letter X, meaning invalid; the check uses the score before rounding.
  26. letter_grade: Whenever the score is text that is wholly a number (e.g. '85', ' 85 ', '1e2'), it is graded as that number.
  27. letter_grade: Whenever the score is NULL, empty text, spaces only or other non-numeric text, the result is NULL.
  28. loyalty_points: Whenever the tier is basic, bronze, an unrecognised name, empty text, NULL or a non-text value, points are 1 per unit of spend (spend 1000 gives 1000).
  29. loyalty_points: Whenever the tier is silver, points are 1.5 per unit of spend (1000 gives 1500); for gold, 2 per unit (1000 gives 2000).
  30. loyalty_points: Whenever the tier is written in different letter case or with spaces around it (GOLD, ' Gold ', Silver), it is recognised as that tier; but spaces inside a name (e.g. 'sil ver') are not, giving the 1-per-unit rate.

  35. loyalty_points: Whenever spend is NULL, empty text or non-numeric text, the result is NULL, whatever the tier.

  37. mask_card: Whenever a card number has at least 12 digits, the result shows the first 6 digits, then one asterisk for every digit in between, then the last 4 digits (4111111111111111 gives 411111******1111).
  38. mask_card: Whenever the card number contains spaces, hyphens or any other non-digit characters, those are removed first and only the digits are counted and shown (4111-1111-1111-1111 and '4111 1111 1111 1111' both give 411111******1111; letters inside are dropped too).

  40. mask_card: Whenever fewer than 12 digits remain after removing non-digits (11 digits, empty text, spaces only, letters only like 'abcd'), the result is the text INVALID.

  51. pct_change: Whenever either value is empty text or non-numeric text, the result is NULL, even when old_value is 0 ('0' to 'abc' gives NULL).
  52. pct_change: Whenever a value is text that is wholly a number (e.g. '100', ' 100 ', '1e2'), it is used as that number.
  53. ship_cost: Whenever the weight is above 0, the charge is a base of 300 cents plus a per-block charge for each started 500 g (weight divided by 500, rounded up): 100 cents per block in zone 1, 180 in zone 2 and 260 in zone 3.
  54. ship_cost: Whenever the weight is exactly on a 500 g multiple it counts that many blocks (500 g in zone 1 gives 400); one gram more starts a new block (501 g gives 500); even 0.5 g counts as one block.
  55. ship_cost: Whenever the weight is above 20000 g (20000 g exactly is not above), a flat surcharge of 2000 cents is added (20000 g zone 1 gives 4300; 20001 g zone 1 gives 6400; 20001 g zone 3 gives 12960).

  57. ship_cost: Whenever the zone is written as 2.0, '2' or ' 2 ', it counts as zone 2.
  58. ship_cost: Whenever the weight is 0 or negative, the charge is 0 (no base charge) for any valid zone, including an out-of-range zone.
  59. ship_cost: Whenever the weight or the zone is NULL, empty text or non-numeric text, the result is NULL, even if the other input is 0 or negative.
  60. ship_cost: Whenever the weight is text that is wholly a number (e.g. '500'), it is used as that number.
  61. slug: Whenever a title is given, it is turned into lower case, and each run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 (spaces, tabs, line breaks, punctuation, underscores, hyphens, ampersands, symbols) is replaced by a single hyphen ('Hello,   World!' gives hello-world; 'a_b-c' gives a-b-c; 'a--b' gives a-b).
